reading: Telehouse is a carrier neutral colocation data center provider and a subsidiary of KDDI Corporation, one of Japan's largest telecommunications companies. Telehouse America operates the New York Teleport facility referenced in this registry, part of a group of interconnected Telehouse data centers in the New York metro area that together form a major internet exchange and carrier hub for the northeastern United States. Telehouse has continued to expand its US footprint through acquisition, including KDDI's roughly one billion dollar purchase of Allied Properties' Canadian and US data center portfolio, reported in industry press, extending Telehouse's presence beyond its original New York cluster. As a long established carrier neutral operator, Telehouse markets its facilities on dense interconnection, meet me room access, and proximity to major network peering points rather than on hyperscale cloud capacity, positioning it alongside operators like Equinix and CoreSite in the New York colocation market rather than alongside hyperscale cloud providers. No specific critical IT megawattage figure for the New York Teleport facility was found published on Telehouse's own site during this research, so that field is left unspecified rather than estimated. Telehouse's own site and its Wikipedia entry were used as the primary sources for this profile, with trade press used only for context on recent acquisition activity.
